candidates.detail: IA-D01 defines these as distinct. This implies the air loss could originate in either location or at their interface, complicating origin identification without additional data.

candidates.label: Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release.
candidates.detail: IA-D01 states that Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary, and Maintenance (M-A) accepts it later. At 10:00 AM, M-A's signature was not yet obtained per IA-S02, suggesting incomplete handover of control or information.

candidates.label: Utilities air gallery serves RHOB process area and distributes instrument air to the receiving header H-R.
candidates.detail: The directory identifies RHOB as a local area name for records, not an individual compressor. The gallery supplies 1SC dryer group D-101 and routes air to RHOB.

candidates.label: Local indication P-R at RHOB receiving header H-R normally shows normal pressure band.
candidates.detail: The point register maps AL-44 to the receiving-header pressure condition. Normal operation implies a 'normal band' reading before 10:00 AM (6.8 bar).

candidates.label: Pressure upstream of distribution routes (P-U) remained stable at 6.9 bar during the event window.
candidates.detail: Measurements show P-U was constant at 6.8–6.9 bar from 09:54 to 10:08, indicating supply pressure did not drop significantly upstream of RHOB.

candidates.label: Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time.
candidates.detail: The work package cover explicitly states 'Maintenance acceptance signature: not yet signed' when the incident occurred, meaning formal boundary release had not been granted.

candidates.label: No line opening was authorized at the time of interruption.
candidates.detail: Shift log entry at 10:02 AM explicitly records 'No line opening authorized' while work was paused and issue under review.

candidates.label: Area directory does not establish valve positions or pressure availability at any given time.
candidates.detail: The area and service directory is a location index only; it explicitly states it 'does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.'

candidates.label: Desk entries do not log every field operation or identify the point of interruption.
candidates.detail: The shift log excerpt states 'desk entries do not log every field operation' and explicitly notes they 'do not identify the point at which the air supply was interrupted.'

candidates.label: No documented confirmation of understanding regarding root cause assessment or response steps is present.
candidates.detail: Evidence shows no interview concerning fatigue, workload, intent, or discussion confirming how the interruption was handled beyond pausing work.

candidates.label: RHOB reported an 'air-low' indication and requested Utilities attendance at ~10:00 AM.
candidates.detail: Shift log records RHOB entry stating 'Air-low indication. Local controls showing supply complaints. Requested Utilities attendance.'

candidates.label: Utilities acknowledged receipt of the issue at ~10:02 AM and paused work.
candidates.detail: Shift log records Utilities entry stating 'Work paused. RHOB service issue under review.' following RHOB's request for attendance.

candidates.label: Local indication P-R dropped from 6.8 bar to below alarm threshold (5.0 bar) between 10:00 and 10:03 AM.
candidates.detail: Pressure samples show P-R at 6.8 bar at 09:54, dropping to 5.8 bar at 10:00:11, then 4.1 bar at 10:00:40 (below AL-44 alarm threshold of 4.5 bar).

candidates.label: Alarm AL-44 triggered at 10:00:32 and was acknowledged by Utilities.
candidates.detail: Pressure samples show P-R below alarm threshold starting at 10:00:11. Alarm journal shows occurrence time of 10:00:32, acknowledgment at 10:03:14.

candidates.label: Normal pressure returned at ~10:07 AM after alarm cleared.
candidates.detail: Pressure samples show P-R returning to 6.0 bar by 10:06:20 and normal band (6.8 bar) by 10:06:50. RHOB requested retention of records at this time.

candidates.label: Crew U-A/U-B had current Utilities operating qualification and energy-control authorization.
candidates.detail: Assignment extract lists both operators with 'Current Utilities operating qualification and energy-control authorization' at shift start.

candidates.label: Maintenance receiver M-A had boundary acceptance pending.
candidates.detail: Assignment extract lists M-A with 'boundary acceptance pending' status at shift start, consistent with work package cover noting signature not yet signed.

candidates.label: Work folder WO-527-E was blank at issue time.
candidates.detail: Work package cover attachment index shows 'WO-527-E: Blank at folder issue' for the field execution record, indicating no pre-filled isolation steps or valve states were documented on handover.

candidates.label: Daily work briefing topic line read '1SC dryer work and RHOB service coordination'.
candidates.detail: Assignment extract notes the daily briefing attendance sheet contains no valve-by-valve content, only a general topic line.

candidates.label: Crew U-A/U-B held current operating qualifications at shift start.
candidates.detail: Personnel codes are fictional; no actual employee records reproduced. Qualification status is recorded but not observed performance on the job.

candidates.label: Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time.
candidates.detail: Work-boundary release pending; maintenance receiver M-A had not accepted the boundary when air loss occurred.

candidates.label: Temporary instruction attachment field was blank at issue time.
candidates.detail: No temporary instruction attached to work package cover; ECP-1SC-04 revision 3 issued but no approved temp instruction for this specific boundary change or routing update.

candidates.label: Area directory (IA-D01) does not establish valve positions or pressure availability at any given time.
candidates.detail: Directory is a location index only; cannot confirm if valves were open/closed or which path was active when loss occurred.

candidates.label: Daily work briefing contained no valve-by-valve content.
candidates.detail: Briefing topic line read '1SC dryer work and RHOB service coordination' but did not list specific valves or routing changes affecting the boundary.

candidates.label: No evidence crew received recent change briefing or saw specific configuration drawing used.
candidates.detail: Training extract does not state which configuration drawing the crew saw; no interview concerning fatigue, workload or individual intent included.

candidates.label: Point register maps signals but does not establish state of any distribution valve.
candidates.detail: Register IA-P02 shows P-U and P-R points, AL-44 alarm mapping; explicitly states it does not prove every supply disturbance appears in selected sample export or identify intermediate valves.

candidates.label: RHOB requested Utilities attendance at 10:00; work paused by 10:02.
candidates.detail: Shift log shows RHOB entry 'Air-low indication... Requested Utilities attendance' followed by Utilities entry 'Work paused. RHOB service issue under review.'

candidates.label: Local indication P-R normally shows normal pressure band; upstream P-U remained stable at 6.9 bar.
candidates.detail: Shift log notes morning check showed local air indication in normal band; point register excerpt implies P-U stability while P-R dropped, though exact values not captured continuously.

candidates.label: Potential unrecorded service-routing change or undocumented valve state created a unique hazard scenario.
candidates.detail: Hypothesis that an unrecorded routing change occurred; no evidence confirms such event actually happened. Absence of record does not prove occurrence.

candidates.label: Communication breakdown between Utilities and RHOB may have contributed to delayed response.
candidates.detail: Hypothesis that coordination was impaired; evidence shows request at 10:00 and pause by 10:02, but no record indicates delay beyond normal steps or communication failure.

candidates.label: Transient nature of air pressure loss suggests possible upstream or distribution system issue rather than equipment failure at receiving end.
candidates.detail: Hypothesis based on transient event; records do not establish where interruption began (source vs. distribution). Transient nature alone does not support this inference without additional evidence.
